criteria.title: Selected profile versus prospective general receipt; no label/env/receipt grants effect

sourceFacts.fact: resolveHtmlJobSyntheticProfile returns null when NODE_ENV is production or CVF_NCR_HTML_JOB_PROFILE is not LOCAL_SYNTHETIC; it layers on the draft resolver.
resolveHtmlDraftSyntheticProfile is server-only (comment L9: no request field can select it); needs CVF_NCR_DRAFT_PROFILE, an absolute canonical root, a run id and a marker file.
With the selected profile the route takes selectedPrincipal and returns receipt status NOT_CONFIGURED without calling fetchGovernanceReceipt.
Existing focused test asserts the selected profile never reads CVF_SERVICE_TOKEN and never fetches a receipt.
In the general branch the receipt hop fires whenever the env-derived URL resolves to an absolute URL; no profile opt-in and no operation record exist.
governanceState is only a label; the HTML build and the hop are not gated on any receipt decision.

rootDesign: Selected LOCAL_SYNTHETIC/no-receipt stays the profile; general receipt is a separately admitted branch; label/env/ALLOW/operator copy is not permission.
auditAssumptions: A new server-only operation profile (name proposed: CVF_NCR_RECEIPT_OPERATION_PROFILE) gates the controlled branch in addition to the URL env; its exact name is a BUILD detail.
criteria.consequence: Property holds for the selected branch and can hold for a new controlled branch. It does NOT hold for the legacy general branch today: an authenticated caller plus an absolute URL env is enough to emit the hop with no operation record (finding F-01). Deployment values are unread, so reachability in any real deployment is UNKNOWN.
criteria.heldBuild: None for the synthetic proof. Legacy-branch disposition is held (HQ4).

criteria.title: Immutable server-resolved operation envelope; concrete producer/lookup/transport or held

sourceFacts.fact: Export DTO has exactly seven fields; unknown keys are rejected (400 Unknown artifact export field); no job or operation reference is accepted.
The client holds the job reference from prepareJob when it calls fetch(exportEndpoint) but sends only the seven-field body; the reference is not transmitted.
prepareJob mints a fresh crypto.randomUUID jobId on every call and creates a job with a goal, criteria and the request.
Existing job owner: owner-scoped CREATE_JOB/LINK_VERSION/ACCEPT_VERSION and GET job/version/decision; principal comes from normalPrincipal(session).
Owner-scoped lookups getJob and getVersion join request/html hashes; only usable when jobDecisions is true.
createJob requires jobDecisions and a sourceRecordId starting with ncr-synthetic-; no general or production job store exists.

JOB_EFFECTS is the closed list LOCAL_HTML_BUILD, LOCAL_DRAFT_SAVE, LOCAL_SYNTHETIC_REVIEW; the job schema uses exact keys, so a job can neither carry effectKind/endpoint/config nor authorise an outbound receipt effect.
requestIdentity is the fixed-order seven-field identity; job.requestSha256 = sha256(requestIdentity(request)) (S14 L72), so the route can recompute the same value from its own validated body.
General auth yields actorId only; a service-token caller has no user/org/team, a session caller exposes orgId/teamId only through the returned session object that route.ts does not use.
The engine ledger path is an engine-process env value (CVF_GOVERNANCE_LEDGER_PATH); nothing in the Web path can observe it.

rootDesign: Envelope binds schema/config/policy/transform revisions, effectKind, actor, source/job/frozen input, output identity where available, endpoint/store identity, secret reference, payload digest, risk and limits; no untrusted field grants authority; the audit must choose a concrete existing-owner producer/lookup/transport or hold.
auditAssumptions: Producer: inside the export route, after authentication, from server-resolved profile + normalPrincipal(session) + server-recomputed request identity + owner-scoped HtmlDraftSnapshotStore.getJob/getVersion (selectors are lookup keys only).

Transport: two selector headers (job id, source record id) set at the useHtmlBuildAttempts fetch site; body fields rejected because the seven-field DTO is mirrored by REQUEST_KEYS (S15 L8) and requestValid (S14 L23-L27).
Controlled branch requires a session principal; service-token-only callers are denied.
Endpoint and backend-store identity can only be declared configuration (unattested): the Web side cannot read the engine ledger path.
criteria.consequence: A concrete existing-owner producer/lookup/transport exists for the FIRST SYNTHETIC PROOF only. Held: (a) a non-synthetic producer (no general job store), (b) attestation of endpoint/backend-store identity, (c) any service-token-only caller. The Root candidate manifest omits the client transport site (finding F-13).
criteria.heldBuild: Held for any non-synthetic or production scope; open for the synthetic offline proof once HQ2 and HQ5 are decided.

criteria.title: Distinct logical effect identity, envelope digest, attempt ID, receipt ID; unresolved effect not escapable

sourceFacts.fact: Each Build creates a new job with a client-generated random UUID.
createJob accepts any new valid job id for the owner; a second job with the same frozen request is accepted.
Attempt id is built inside the helper as artifact-proof-<slug of client receiptAnchor>-<Date.now()>: not caller-injectable, millisecond granularity, client-influenced.
receiptId is set equal to requestId, so attempt id and receipt id are the same string today.
The helper artifactId is slugify(receiptAnchor), a client-supplied field.
The response carries no engine-issued receipt identifier separate from request_id.
Engine ledger event holds request_id, decision, timestamp, cvf_phase, cvf_risk_level; no artifact_id and no payload digest.

Existing route tests pin receiptId and governanceReceiptAttemptId to the artifact-proof-<slug>- pattern and authenticate the general branch with a signed service token (no user, org or team), so the default helper path must keep attempt id equal to receipt id for legacy callers.

rootDesign: Logical key covers actor/source/job/frozen input/effectKind; envelope additionally binds version/output/config/endpoint; changed endpoint/config or regenerated version cannot escape an unresolved prior effect; new intent is separate authority.
auditAssumptions: Smallest alternative: logical key = sha256 of fixed-order [schema, userId, orgId, teamId, sourceRecordId, requestSha256, effectKind]; jobId, versionId, configRevision, endpoint and htmlSha256 are bound in the envelope digest only.
attemptId is allocated by the controlled branch before the hop and injected into the helper; outcomeId is an artifacts-owned record id; no engine-issued receipt id exists to reuse.
Policy for an identical frozen request after RECEIPT_VERIFIED (return the existing record with zero sends, versus deny) is a Root decision; the audit recommends return-existing.
criteria.consequence: As written, a key that includes the job id is unique per Build click, so duplicate protection would be vacuous and any user action could mint a fresh key. Dependent BUILD (key derivation) is held until Local ratifies the amended key; the envelope digest, attempt id and outcome id separation are feasible.
criteria.heldBuild: Key derivation module content held for HQ1.

criteria.title: Single-host non-production synthetic storage; exclusive intent/start/outcome; readback; no delete-retry

sourceFacts.fact: directory(): lstat/realpath checks of root and per-owner directory (name = sha256 of user/org/team), mkdir mode 0o700, symlink and namespace escape rejected.

Exclusive create with flag wx and mode 0o600; EEXIST maps to COLLISION; write plus handle.sync; failures map to UNCONFIRMED/UNAVAILABLE; readback compares JSON before SAVED. Comment L53: even an incomplete prior file consumes the id.
Only the file handle is synced; there is no directory fsync.
readSidecar returns null for missing, empty, oversize, corrupt and symlink cases alike, so ABSENT and UNREADABLE are not distinguishable.
MAX_JOB_METADATA_BYTES is 16384 for sidecars.
The class has no delete, unlink or cleanup method and no record-count cap.
list() only returns names that are a UUID plus .json, so operation files with another prefix are not listed as snapshots.

rootDesign: Extend the existing artifacts payload owner; immutable intent, exclusive start, immutable outcome; bounded size; readback before grant; any write problem denies the attempt; incomplete marker consumes the key; no delete-and-retry; no durability or distributed-lock claim.
auditAssumptions: New methods must expose a tri-state read (ABSENT / PRESENT / UNREADABLE) and must never use a validated read as the admission test; wx collision is the authority.
A per-owner record cap and a clear store-full denial are new design items (no cap exists).

Cross-process one-winner behaviour of wx is plausible on one local filesystem but unproven: needs its own two-process fixture. T1B rejected plain rename as CAS; wx creates a new name and never replaces, but T1B did not evaluate it.
Fallback if the two-process fixture fails: the accepted specialised single-host SQLite pattern (S07 L562-L602, L687-L708) in an artifacts-owned file, not a generic engine.
criteria.consequence: Feasible with limits: no directory durability, no power-loss claim, POSIX modes cannot be asserted on this Windows host, TOCTOU between directory() and open remains within a single-user synthetic root.

criteria.title: State proposal PREPARED -> STARTED -> terminal; exclusive start grants one injected invocation

sourceFacts.fact: Existing lifecycle CREATED -> CLAIMED -> EXECUTING -> SUCCEEDED/FAILED/DENIED/UNKNOWN_TERMINAL plus EXPIRED/STALE/ABANDONED_BEFORE_START; terminal states are immutable.
beginPendingExecution consumes a single-use in-process grant and performs a compare-and-swap CLAIMED -> EXECUTING.
The grant is a process-local object tracked in WeakSet/WeakMap and is not serializable, so it cannot survive restart.
resolveAmbiguousExecutingCrash maps an ambiguous execution to UNKNOWN_TERMINAL.

Only the NOT_CONFIGURED return occurs before the fetch call; every later failure (non-ok HTTP, bad JSON, abort, thrown fetch error) collapses into UNAVAILABLE/INVALID_RESPONSE/TIMED_OUT without telling pre-send from post-send.
Reusable pattern: a mandatory boundary callback awaits one fallible admission and then accounts synchronously, so the invocation is only reachable through it.
Exclusive create gives a single winner per record name.

rootDesign: PREPARED -> exclusive STARTED -> RECEIPT_VERIFIED | DENIED | FAILED_BEFORE_SEND | OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; only the verified exclusive start reaches one injected invocation; restart/existing STARTED is unknown; outcome-write failure after send stays unknown; negative record is not proof of non-execution; FAILED_BEFORE_SEND needs a mechanically proven boundary.
auditAssumptions: States are records: intent file = PREPARED, start file = STARTED, outcome file = terminal; a start without outcome is derived UNKNOWN.
A process-local single-use StartGrant (private-constructor token + WeakSet, same pattern as ResumeAuthorityGrant) is the only way into the injected invoker.

FAILED_BEFORE_SEND is limited to: wrapper failure before the invoker is entered, or the invoker returning the typed NOT_CONFIGURED; TIMED_OUT, UNAVAILABLE, INVALID_RESPONSE and any thrown error map to OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
DENIED is persisted only after PREPARED; a denial before PREPARED writes nothing and consumes nothing because no send is possible.
criteria.consequence: Mapping is implementable. The helper must gain an injected-invoker seam and a typed pre-send return; HTTP failures cannot be classified as pre-send.

criteria.title: Reconcile with same operation/config/store/actor and expected IDs; lookup does not Build/Save/invoke

sourceFacts.fact: Engine HTTP surface is health, evaluate, approve, ledger?limit (tail window) and risk-convert; there is no read-by-request-id endpoint.
Web ledger route clamps the window to 1..500 and needs a session or the service token.
SqliteLedger.lookup_request_id exists in Python only.
The historical W05 exact-id check opened the SQLite store directly through SqliteLedger (file-level), not through HTTP.
The default JSON ledger appends every event with no request_id uniqueness.
The SQLite ledger has a UNIQUE request_id and returns the existing block only for byte-identical event bytes; otherwise it raises.
The event contains a wall-clock timestamp, so a same-id replay is not byte-identical.
Helper timeout defaults to 4000 ms.
Engine client timeout defaults to 5000 ms, so a commit after the helper has given up is structurally reachable.
Lost response, malformed response and timeout all end as non-PRESENT statuses that keep the attempt id.

rootDesign: Reconcile with the same operation/config/store/actor and expected receipt/attempt IDs; lookup never Builds, Saves or invokes; failures and mismatches preserve unknown/not-approved; a new attempt needs a separate contract.
auditAssumptions: Option B (first proof): read local records plus the existing read-only governanceLedger tail window; presence of the expected request_id can be recorded, absence proves nothing.
Option A (held): add a read-by-id engine endpoint and a Web proxy route; adds Python and Web owners outside the Root candidate manifest.
Option C rejected: file-level reads of the engine store couple Web to a secret path and cannot be authenticated.
criteria.consequence: No authenticated exact-id lookup exists over HTTP. Option B cannot detect a wrong store or bind artifact/payload (ledger event has neither). Local-record reconcile and fail-closed unknown handling are supportable now; durable remote reconcile is held.
criteria.heldBuild: Remote reconcile held for HQ3; local-record reconcile is not held.

criteria.title: Authentication resolved per hop; export proof is not durable admission

sourceFacts.fact: Export auth accepts a signed service token (HMAC over timestamp and body, 5 minute window) or a session; it reads CVF_SERVICE_TOKEN before the session branch.
The service-token replay ledger is an in-memory Map, bounded, process-local.
Selected profile uses same-origin check, requireAdminApiSession without break-glass, and normalPrincipal.
The receipt fetch sends only Content-Type and an optional x-cvf-service-token header; no cookies are forwarded.
The evaluate route authorises a session or a plain equality of the presented token with the configured token (not the HMAC scheme).
The Web-to-engine fetch sends only Content-Type; no credential.
Grep over the whole file for Depends/Authorization/api_key/middleware/CORS/x-cvf/token returned no hit; lines 60-255 were read and show no authentication construct.
normalPrincipal rejects break-glass, impersonation and expired sessions.

rootDesign: Export proof is not durable admission; receipt fetch does not forward cookies; destination, secret reference, scope and receiving auth must be bound before the call; no env, secret or credential inspection.
auditAssumptions: Envelope stores only the secret reference name and a coarse scope label (service token is not route-scoped); declared, not attested.
criteria.consequence: Hop 1 (export to evaluate) needs a configured service token equal on both sides; hop 2 (evaluate to engine) is unauthenticated at source level, so confinement is an unproven deployment assumption. Actual URL, token and network values are UNKNOWN (not inspected).
criteria.heldBuild: None for synthetic proof; real destination binding remains an action-specific checkpoint.

criteria.title: Route risk R1 versus receipt payload REVIEW/R0 needs explicit disposition

sourceFacts.fact: Route registry declares /api/artifacts/export with riskLevel R1.
The receipt payload hard-codes cvf_phase REVIEW and cvf_risk_level R0 with no stated rationale.
The helper validates the response risk only against ^R[0-4]$ and does not compare it with the declared request level.
The engine ledger records the request-declared cvf_risk_level and cvf_phase as supplied; routing uses the evaluated risk_score.
The engine phase authority table is keyed A to E; the literal REVIEW is not a key (effect on enrich_result not read).
fetchGovernanceReceipt has a single call site, so a default-preserving parameter can leave legacy bytes unchanged.

rootDesign: Controlled branch declares R1 unless a stronger source-owner rationale exists; preserve legacy; no policy mutation; no fake runtime approval.
auditAssumptions: Add an optional declaredRisk parameter to the helper, default R0; controlled branch passes R1.
No stronger rationale for R0 was found in the files read.
criteria.consequence: Supported. Behavioural effect of R1 on engine decisions is unverified beyond the ledger metadata (routing code read only in part); decision to confirm R1 is HQ7.

criteria.title: Stop/timeout are local observations; unknown cost stays unknown; excerpt is code units; labels separate

sourceFacts.fact: Client Stop calls AbortController.abort on the browser fetch only.
The route never reads request.signal; the hop is not tied to the incoming request.
The hop has its own timer-driven AbortController; timeout is 4000 ms default, configurable 1000-30000 ms.
Excerpt is sourceContent.slice(0, 500): 500 UTF-16 code units, not bytes.
governanceReceiptAttemptId is returned when present; governanceState keeps DRAFT_UNACCEPTED unless a legacy APPROVED decision and passing checks.
Rendered HTML states a receipt anchor and presentation do not establish approval or acceptance.
The only call/quota accounting is for provider calls on /api/execute; the receipt hop has no cost or call meter.

rootDesign: Local Stop/timeouts are local observations; distinguish requested cancel, confirmed remote cancel, credential revoke and past effects/billing; unknown cost is unknown; keep artifact/draft/person acceptance separate.
auditAssumptions: Forwarding request.signal is not adopted: it would add a cancel claim without remote confirmation.
Revoke is prospective only (profile disable), never retroactive.
criteria.consequence: Supported. Past remote effects, billing and remote cancellation are unobservable from this source; any text claiming otherwise would be unsupported.

criteria.title: Existing owners compared; none is a drop-in permit; reuse mechanisms; no fabricated approval or parallel engine

sourceFacts.fact: Pending payload requires approvalId, approvalRequestHash and a snapshot that must hash-match; claim requires an approved ApprovalRequestRecord with actor and policy fingerprint checks.
Environment identity must say single_process_non_production.
SQLite store: WAL, synchronous FULL, busy timeout, unique create with readback, conditional UPDATE compare-and-swap; table is shaped for PendingAgentExecutionRecord only.
Composition is declared unwired to any route, provider, audit or barrel.
Only importers of the composition are the local harness and tests (grep): no route or artifacts caller.
T1B decision: single host only, forbidden imports of execute route, approvals route and provider admission, route reopen gates required.
Provider attempt admission reserves per-identity quota in a per-request in-memory ledger and counts call starts.
NON_VISION_EXECUTION_PATH_SELECTION is direct; the gateway port is for provider text execution.
Engine ledger is written by the evaluate call itself, i.e. after the effect, as downstream evaluation evidence.

rootDesign: Compare owners; none is a drop-in artifact permit; reuse compatible mechanisms; never fabricate an ApprovalRequestRecord, relax frozen guards, reuse quota as durable admission or build a parallel generic engine.
auditAssumptions: Reusable by pattern only: compare-and-swap one-winner, UNKNOWN terminal semantics, single-use in-process grant, zero-grant failure containment, schema-version fail-closed read.
canonicalDigest is exported by the pending core, but importing it pulls approvals types into artifacts; a local fixed-order identity (as requestIdentity does) avoids the cross-owner dependency.
criteria.consequence: Comparison supports the Root stance; no owner substitutes for an artifacts-domain record. The artifacts operation record is a new artifacts-owned record type, not a second generic engine.

criteria.title: Retention, tombstones, store-full behaviour, safe-copy migration, runtime disable

sourceFacts.fact: Draft TTL is 24 hours and validateSnapshot rejects an expired record.
validateJob, validateVersion and validateDecision also reject expired records; the reads then return null (S11 L109), indistinguishable from absence.
No deletion or expiry sweeper exists in the store; files persist.
A write failure other than EEXIST returns UNAVAILABLE, so ENOSPC denies; no capacity count exists.
When the job profile resolves to null the route does not stop: it falls through to authorizeRouteGovernanceProof and the legacy receipt path.
Disabled job profile only changes the jobs route to 503 JOB_PROFILE_DISABLED.

rootDesign: No retention expiry may silently recycle unknown keys; define denial/tombstone and bounded store-full; draft TTL is not dedupe retention; safe-copy migration/rollback and runtime disable are separate; disable new effects without deleting unresolved facts.
auditAssumptions: Admission authority is wx existence only; expiry-bearing validators are never used for admission.
Records have no TTL and no deletion path; a tombstone is just the terminal DENIED/UNKNOWN record; per-owner cap with deny-on-full.
A declared-but-disabled or invalid operation profile must deny the hop and must not fall through to the legacy branch; legacy remains reachable only where the profile variable is undeclared.
Safe-copy migration proof: copy the store directory, change nothing in the original, verify record hashes, run disabled profile against the copy.
criteria.consequence: Retention and fall-through rules are not present in source and must be ratified; without the fall-through rule, turning the profile off re-enables the legacy path (F-08).

criteria.title: Executable-development manifest and finite fault proof plan before any source work order

sourceFacts.fact: general_source soft 700 / hard 1000 lines; test_code soft 800 / hard 1200; export/route.ts is 389 lines and the snapshot store 181.
The compressed-statement rule fires only for a changed file within near_hard_margin (25) lines of the hard threshold, so it does not apply to files of a few hundred lines.
job-profile.test.ts is the regression oracle that the selected profile never fetches a receipt.
Client fetch site that must carry the selectors is not in the Root candidate manifest.

rootDesign: Manifest of every changed/new/read-only owner with action, reason, dependency, size, phase and effect boundary, plus an offline fixture proof plan; no test creation or execution now.
auditAssumptions: Size figures are estimates from read line counts; nothing was built or measured.
Registry/generated needs (corpus scan registry aggregate, public catalog update at closure) are flagged for Local; not verified.
criteria.consequence: Manifest and proof plan delivered in this evidence file (sections futureManifest and proofPlan). The Root candidate manifest needs amendments (F-13).

findings.finding: Legacy general receipt branch is env-switched and leaves no operation record; a controlled branch does not protect a deployment where the legacy branch stays reachable.
findings.consequence: Cutover must make legacy unreachable where the controlled profile is declared (HQ4).

findings.finding: Locked logical key includes the job id, but each Build mints a new random job id, so the key is unique per click.
Engine ledger events have no artifact id or payload digest and carry a wall-clock timestamp; the default JSON ledger does not enforce request id uniqueness.
findings.consequence: Remote reconcile can bind request id and decision only; duplicate protection is ledger-configuration dependent.

findings.finding: No authenticated read-by-id exists over HTTP; historical W05 used file-level store inspection.
findings.consequence: D06 DESIGN_GAP; option B presence-only or option A new owners (HQ3).

findings.finding: Attempt id equals receipt id and is generated inside the helper from a client-influenced slug and Date.now.
findings.consequence: Helper needs an injected attempt id and a separately named outcome id.

findings.finding: Helper timeout (4 s) is shorter than the engine client timeout (5 s) by default.
findings.consequence: A commit after the caller times out is reachable by construction; unknown-outcome handling is not optional.

findings.finding: The store's sidecar read collapses missing, corrupt and expired records into null.
findings.consequence: Admission must rest on wx collision with a tri-state read, never on validated reads.

findings.finding: Disabling the job profile returns the export route to the legacy branch rather than stopping receipts.
findings.consequence: A declared-but-disabled operation profile must deny, not fall through (HQ4).

findings.finding: Engine hop carries no credential and the engine server shows no authentication construct; export-side service-token replay protection is process-local.
findings.src: S05 L61-L66; S28 whole-file grep; S23 L47
findings.consequence: Per-hop binding is declared configuration, not attested.

findings.finding: Evaluate route compares the presented token with plain equality while the export route uses constant-time HMAC verification.
findings.consequence: Weaker scheme on hop 1; scope is not narrowed per route.

findings.finding: Only the file handle is synced; POSIX file modes cannot be asserted on this Windows host.
findings.consequence: D04 durability and mode claims stay unproven; proof limited to behaviour.

findings.finding: The receipt payload carries only content, so the engine records actor system for every receipt.
findings.consequence: Actor attribution lives only in the artifacts-domain record.

findings.finding: Root candidate manifest omits the client transport site, a testable branch module, a profile resolver, a helper parity test and conditional registry or catalog updates.
findings.consequence: Manifest amended in this evidence (M05-M10, M13, M17, M18).

findings.finding: The payload phase literal REVIEW is not a key of the engine phase table (A to E).
findings.consequence: Effect on enrichment unverified; not changed.
